## Technology Stack

### Frontend
- HTML5
- CSS3 (following Michelin Design System)
- Vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks)

### Backend
- Python 3.10+
- FastAPI
- SQLAlchemy ORM
- SQLite database

## Pages

| Page | Description | Navigation Bar | Auth Required |
|------|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| Login | User authentication | No | No |
| Landing | Welcome page with personalized greeting | Yes | Yes |
| Dashboard | IDMS data table and API usage statistics | Yes | Yes |
| Audit Log | User activity history | Yes | Yes |
| Settings | User profile management | Yes | Yes |
| 404 | Error page | No | No |

## Setup Instructions

### Backend Setup

1. Navigate to the backend directory:
   ```powershell
   cd backend
   ```

2. Create a virtual environment:
   ```powershell
   python -m venv venv
   ```

3. Activate the virtual environment:
   ```powershell
   .\venv\Scripts\Activate
   ```

4. Install dependencies:
   ```powershell
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

5. Run the development server:
   ```powershell
   uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
   ```

### Frontend Setup

The frontend is static HTML/CSS/JS and can be served by any web server.

For development, you can use Python's built-in HTTP server:

```powershell
cd frontend
python -m http.server 8080
```

Or use VS Code Live Server extension.

## API Documentation

Once the backend is running, visit:
- Swagger UI: http://localhost:8000/docs
- ReDoc: http://localhost:8000/redoc

## Design System

This project follows the Michelin Design System color scheme:
- Primary Blue: #27509b
- Yellow: #fce500
- Dark Blue: #1a3a6e

Reference: https://designsystem.michelin.com/colors

## Development Notes

- All pages except Login and 404 include the collapsible navigation bar
- Settings page is accessed via profile icon in the top-right corner
- API usage is tracked for dashboard statistics
- All user actions are logged in the audit log

# Website Requirements

S26 – MICHELIN X CLEMSON CAPSTONE REQ SHEET

## Contents

- Introduction
   - Objective
- Requirements
   - Frontend
   - Backend
   - Database
- Structure
   - Login
   - Navigation
      - Common Layout
   - Landing Page
   - Dashboard
   - Audit Log
   - Settings
   - 404 Page
- Helpful Links


## Introduction

The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they’re already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.

### Objective

The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
phases

_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_

## Requirements

### Frontend

The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
and CSS.

### Backend

The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

### Database

Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.


## Structure

### Login

```
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
```
### Navigation

```
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
```
#### Common Layout

```
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and
industry-standard look.

You're hitting a build for pydantic-core that requires Rust because your current Python (cp313 / 3.13) doesn't have a prebuilt wheel for that package. Two fixes: install Rust/cargo or use a Python version with prebuilt wheels (recommended: 3.11 or 3.12). Steps below (concise).

1) Verify current venv Python
```powershell
python -V
python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
```

2) Recommended fix — recreate venv with Python 3.11 (install 3.11 from python.org first), then install requirements:
```powershell
# from backend folder
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .\venv
py -3.11 -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
```

3) Alternative: install Rust toolchain (if you prefer to keep Python 3.13)
- Install Rust from https://rustup.rs (download/run the Windows installer), restart shell so cargo is on PATH, then:
```powershell
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
```

4) If uvicorn still uses the wrong interpreter, always start it with the venv Python:
```powershell
python -m uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
```

If you want, tell me which option you prefer (install Python 3.11 or install Rust) and I’ll give exact commands for that path.

# Website Requirements

S26 – MICHELIN X CLEMSON CAPSTONE REQ SHEET

## Contents

- Introduction
   - Objective
- Requirements
   - Frontend
   - Backend
   - Database
- Structure
   - Login

      - Common Layout
   - Landing Page
   - Dashboard
   - Audit Log
   - Settings

- Helpful Links


## Introduction

The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they’re already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.

### Objective

The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
phases

_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_

## Requirements

### Frontend

The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
and CSS.

### Backend

The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

### Database

Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.


## Structure

### Login

```
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
```
### Navigation

```
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
```
#### Common Layout

```
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and
industry-standard look.
The Setting Page should be accessible from the same pages but via a profile icon in
the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar
```
### Landing Page

```
The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon
and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user’s name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
```
### Dashboard

```
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
of API calls by page.
```

### Audit Log

```
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
table in the database.
```
### Settings

```
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
```
### 404 Page

```
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request
```

# Website Requirements

S26 – MICHELIN X CLEMSON CAPSTONE REQ SHEET

## Contents

- Introduction
   - Objective
- Requirements
   - Frontend
   - Backend
   - Database
- Structure
   - Login
   - Navigation
      - Common Layout
   - Landing Page
   - Dashboard
   - Audit Log
   - Settings
   - 404 Page
- Helpful Links


## Introduction

The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they’re already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.

### Objective

The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
phases

_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_

## Requirements

### Frontend

The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
and CSS.

### Backend

The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

### Database

Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.


## Structure

### Login

```
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
```
### Navigation

```
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
```
#### Common Layout

```
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and
industry-standard look.
The Setting Page should be accessible from the same pages but via a profile icon in
the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar
```
### Landing Page

```
The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon
and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user’s name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
```
### Dashboard

```
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
of API calls by page.
```

### Audit Log

```
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
table in the database.
```
### Settings

```
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
```
### 404 Page

```
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request
```

The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing. ### Objective The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._ After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other phases _*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_ ## Requirements ### Frontend The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS, and CSS. ### Backend The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross- origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development. ### Database Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend. ## Structure ### Login ``` The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should route the user to the Landing Page ``` ### Navigation ``` The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages of the app should react to this properly ``` #### Common Layout ``` The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and industry-standard look. The Setting Page should be accessible from the same pages but via a profile icon in the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar ``` ### Landing Page ``` The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use the database to retrieve the user’s name and include it in the welcome message to make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar ``` ### Dashboard ``` The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here (Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns of API calls by page. ``` ### Audit Log ``` The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log table in the database. ``` ### Settings ``` The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally). ``` ### 404 Page ``` The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request ``` ## Helpful Links Michelin Color Scheme - https://designsystem.michelin.com/colors Figma Workspace – https://www.figma.com/design/E7SV3uBmFOCVnXPrbTTeKQ/S26- Michelin-Capstone?node-id=0-1&t=GNDtaq06lk6hjzDn- 1 Kanban Board – https://trello.com/invite/b/696656324d8f70a5590b0214/ATTI6c1ab40d68bb8f1a0a5f b438d932D4BAE073/s26-michelin-capstone The current date is February 12, 2026. 1. **`box-shadow: 0 0 15px 5px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3);`**
   - `0 0`: No horizontal or vertical offset, so the shadow is centered around the icon.
   - `15px`: The blur radius, which determines how soft the shadow edges are.
   - `5px`: The spread radius, which determines how far the shadow extends outward.
   - `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3)`: A semi-transparent white color for the shadow.

2. **`transform: scale(1.1);`**
   - Slightly enlarges the profile icon when hovered, giving it a more interactive feel.
